title: Negation-class parallel Pollard rho on P-256 with a global work meter (class walk of 1c600df4 adapted to P-256)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production P-256 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (negation-class parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=2048 adding walk on classes {P,-P} keyed by x, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes routed to 2^16 storage nodes each natively addressable below 2^57 bytes, re-walk solving), adapted from the class walk of submission 1c600df4 (mpjunior92) as ported in our a188e335, halts on every run after at most 2^129.46 units of C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions because a global work meter charges every action before it runs; all P-256 arithmetic is charged through itemised analytic instruction allowances (M=512, A=64, I=2^19; 3.6 units per step). It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random mapping on N=(r-1)/2 classes with Brent-Pollard correction and a 5% slowdown allowance; index, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random), supported by toy runs. Peak memory < 2^73 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^60 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production P-256 checks of every identity the walk uses; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (T_c census, pipeline success with node routing, long-trail trap test).
